subject: MSA + Order Form — SLA redlines (uptime, credits, maintenance)
messages:
From: Jamie Holt <jamie@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acme.com>, Legal Counsel <legal@acme.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MSA & Order Form - SLA items

Marissa —

Thanks for the draft MSA + order form. Our procurement and legal teams flagged the SLA section for a few clarifications before we can circulate this internally:

1) Uptime target: we need confirmation that the 99.9% uptime is measured per calendar month and whether regional availability splits (us/eu/apac) will be considered separately.

2) Service credits: the credit formula in section 4.2 looks ambiguous around partial-month credits and aggregation across impacted customers.

3) Response times: for P1 incidents we require a 30-minute initial response and a 4-hour mitigation window for enterprise seats — is that something Redwood can commit to?

4) Maintenance windows: we prefer maintenance to be restricted to a single weekly 4-hour window per region; any emergency maintenance must be notified 72 hours in advance and not count towards downtime.

Can you confirm or propose language so we can close this out? Attaching the redline suggestions we prepared.

—Jamie
VP, Infrastructure — Acme Logistics

---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Holt <jamie@acme.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form - SLA items

Hi Jamie — thanks for the clear note and for the redline pass. Quick answers up front, then next steps: 

• Uptime measurement: We measure availability per account per region on a rolling calendar-month basis. We can make regional metrics explicit in the order form (e.g., 99.9% per region) — happy to add that.

• Service credits: current formula is tiered and pro-rated; Kimberly (legal) and I will propose exact wording to make partial-month scenarios explicit and to cap credits at the agreed SLA slab.

• Response times: our standard enterprise response commitment today is Initial Response = 60 minutes for P1, Mitigation Target = 8 hours. Engineering has pushed back on 30/4 for general availability due to on-call staffing assumptions, but we can propose a modified offer: 30-minute initial response + 6-hour mitigation for Dedicated customers, with escalations routed to a named on-call. Aditya — can you confirm feasibility for Acme's expected commit?

• Maintenance: we can add a clause that limits planned maintenance to one weekly 4-hour regional window and requires 72-hour notice for non-emergency maintenance. For emergency maintenance (security patches or regulator-mandated fixes) we will notify as soon as feasible and exclude unavoidable emergency windows from credit calculations.

Attached are Redwood's redline suggestions (MSA and Order Form v3) — Kimberly, please review the credit and definition language; happy to take a short call if helpful.

Next steps: Kimberly to send clean suggested language on credits and definitions; Aditya to confirm operational feasibility of the 30/6 proposal for Dedicated. I will then circulate a counter-redline for Acme to review.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_MSA_redline_20261018.pdf (summary), OrderForm_Redwood_v3_changes.docx

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form - SLA items (legal redline suggestions)

Marissa / Aditya —

I reviewed both Acme's notes and Marissa's proposed approach. High-level redline suggestions below that should be safe/legal while keeping commercial scope intact:

1) Uptime metric: "Availability" defined as successful inference API responses within the applicable service (exclude scheduled maintenance and agreed emergency maintenance). We should explicitly state measurement methodology (per-region, per-calendar-month, 5-minute polling). This prevents ambiguity on partial outages and avoids double-counting overlapping incidents.

2) Service Credits: propose structured slab language:
  - <99.9% to >=99.0% = 10% monthly fee credit
  - <99.0% to >=95.0% = 25% monthly fee credit
  - <95.0% = 45% monthly fee credit
Cap credits at 100% of the monthly recurring charges for the impacted service. Introduce a mechanism for customers to request a claims investigation within 30 days of the SLA reporting.

3) Response Time (P1): accept the Dedicated compromise — Initial Response within 30 minutes, Mitigation Target within 6 hours for Dedicated capacity customers; for Hosted customers keep Initial Response = 60 minutes / Mitigation = 8 hours. Add: "Initial response" means a named on-call engineer has acknowledged the incident and provided a mitigation ETA.

4) Maintenance windows: add required notice (72 hours) for planned maintenance and allow a single weekly 4-hour maintenance window per region. For changes that impact availability (e.g., major kernel or instance reboots) include an explicit runbook handoff requirement: Redwood will provide written runbook and rollback plan 48 hours prior to scheduled maintenance if requested by customer.

5) Evidence and measurement: propose adding a clause that Redwood will make historical availability reports for the affected month available via the Console and provide CSV export for customer review. If Acme requests deeper evidence (logs/KV caches), require an NDA addendum before sharing raw telemetry.

I attached a tracked-changes doc with exact language. Jonas — FYI on operational implications; Aditya please confirm we can guarantee the runbook/rollback commit for dedicated pools.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Kimberly_redlines_SLA_sections.docx

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form - SLA items (ops feasibility)

Quick operational note from infra:

• 30/6 for Dedicated is feasible provided Acme commits to a Dedicated capacity tier with 4x baseline headroom and an agreed on-call escalation path (we'll need named contacts). We cannot support 30/6 on a Hosted best-effort plan.

• Weekly 4-hour maintenance window per region is fine. We'll standardize on the Sunday 02:00-06:00 local region time by default, but can be adjusted per customer agreement.

• Runbooks: we can provide a pre-scheduled runbook and rollback plan 48 hours prior for planned maintenance as Kimberly requested. For emergency patches, we'll provide post-incident notes and an expedited patch report.

I'll provide a short operational note with the headroom requirements and on-call contact template by EOD.

—Aditya
Principal Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Holt <jamie@acme.com>, Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-19T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form - SLA items (next steps)

Jamie — thanks for the quick turnaround and detailed flags. Summary of our current counter-proposal: 

• Measurement: 99.9% per region, per calendar month (5-minute polling).
• Credits: tiered slab formula (10% / 25% / 45%), capped at 100% MRC, claims window 30 days.
• Response: Dedicated customers — Initial 30 minutes / Mitigation 6 hours; Hosted — Initial 60 minutes / Mitigation 8 hours.
• Maintenance: 1x weekly 4-hour window per region with 72-hour notice for planned maintenance; runbook/rollback docs 48 hours prior on request.

Action items:
1) Kimberly to share the tracked-change MSA + Order Form redline to Acme by EOD (attached).
2) Aditya to send the Dedicated-headroom template and on-call contact form.
3) Marissa to push the updated doc to HubSpot and send a DocuSign envelope once Acme confirms the language.

If that all sounds good, Jamie — can Procurement confirm whether Acme will sign for Dedicated capacity (we need that to commit to the 30/6 response)? If not, we'll revert to Hosted response SLAs.

I'll schedule a 30-minute wrap-up call tomorrow at 10:00 PT if convenient — invite to follow.

Best,
Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
